A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with readable methods, equations, figures and complete appendices. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Figure 1 and Appendix A.3 numerically evaluate theoretical privacy bounds. Neither the main text nor appendices report optimization experiments, simulated training outcomes or empirical data analysis.

after.justification: The added Figure 2 also evaluates theoretical privacy bounds. The complete paper reports mathematical analysis and numerical illustrations, without original empirical training, simulation or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: Noisy-ZOGD retains its clipped two-point estimator, orthonormal directions, hybrid Gaussian noise and projection. The noise-mixing parameter beta is complemented between v1 Equation (3) and v2 Equation (4), preserving the same algorithm family. The new auxiliary process is a proof device.

E1.justification: Numerical bound evaluation expands from the strongly convex illustration in Figure 1 to smooth, not necessarily convex losses in v2 Figure 2. This is a limited additional numerical scenario; no datasets or applied learning tasks are introduced.

E2.justification: The numerical comparisons retain standard composition and output perturbation as comparators, including in the new Figure 2. Newly cited Bao and Gupta works are discussed but not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Figure 1's settings are retained. New Figure 2 uses plots labeled RDP with alpha=2, d=100000, sigma=0.1 and eta=K=1000, while varying n. Its exact reporting is inconsistent: the caption says DP and n=1000/2000, whereas the plot titles say RDP and n=10000/2000.

E4.justification: Figure 2 adds a numerical illustration of nonconvex privacy-bound saturation and sensitivity to sample size. The utility analysis and comparison of orthonormal versus i.i.d. directions already existed in v1's appendices; their relocation is not a new ablation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, empirical confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Changes to analytical failure-probability accounting belong to the theoretical guarantees.

E6.justification: Figure 1's numerical curves are retained. New Figure 2 reports optimized privacy-bound curves that plateau below standard composition and output perturbation at sufficiently large iteration counts. These are additional results under different conditions, not improved scores for the retained comparison.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.2 changes from conditional RDP on a high-probability event to an explicit DP guarantee with separate privacy-conversion and coupling-failure terms. Its proof replaces shifted-divergence reductions with an auxiliary process, bounded shifts, total-variation control and Gaussian transcript composition. Appendix H adapts the minibatch guarantee, while most utility and i.i.d.-direction derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statement redefine the central analytical contribution: v1 claims a generalization of shifted-divergence analysis, whereas v2 claims a novel coupling construction that bypasses its inapplicable global-Lipschitz requirement. The overarching claims of convergent privacy, hybrid noise and benefits from multiple orthonormal directions remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly identifies the pointwise-versus-global Lipschitz obstruction that invalidates v1's proposed use of shifted-divergence reductions, and explains how coupling separates failure probability from privacy cost. It also adds a privacy-versus-computation interpretation of increasing K. The existing limitations on practical LLM applicability are retained in Appendix A.

D1.justification: The new Figure 2 supplies parameter annotations for an additional numerical accounting example. Existing Figure 1 settings move from Appendix A.3 to Appendix B without substantive changes. No accompanying solver implementation, code-access information or hardware details are added.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds Bao et al. (2025) on multiple public-state update directions and Gupta et al. (2024) on inherent privacy, positioning this work as answering Gupta's additive-noise amplification question. The DPZero citation changes to its later publication; it is not a new comparison method.

P1.justification: The abstract and analytical narrative are substantially rewritten around coupling. The conclusion and limitations are combined in Appendix A, the appendices are reorganized into A–J, and the main proof exposition is replaced. Author affiliations and other front matter also change.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column layout to two columns, with revised typography, running headers and citation styling. v2 adds a full-page Figure 2 containing two logarithmic plots. Figure 1 is retained with resizing and a revised caption.

improvement.justification: The decisive gain is the replacement of v1's unjustified global-Lipschitz step with an explicit coupling and total-variation argument in Theorem 3.2, substantially strengthening the central theoretical contribution and clarifying failure accounting. Local probability/formula transcription errors remain, including in Appendix H, and Figure 2 has conflicting metric and sample-size labels. These defects limit precision but are narrower than the improvement to the central proof strategy.
